"As you are aware we have been asking for your applicants to take academic IELTS to assess their English level to study on our academic Courses.

As we move closer to September and to the release of the diploma results we feel that for those students who can apply for a Tier 4 child student visa we need to relax this requirement and ask students to take our on-line English test. remarks:
[2 Oct 2013]
We will now be processing students in three tranches: December, April, and June.

This should work in the following way: the first deadline will be the first Friday of December of the year before entry; those students who have applied before that date will be looked at and processed in the first round.  All applications which have been received by that first Friday will be sifted through and students will have the results of their application within two weeks after cut-off date. Students will then have a week to decide whether to accept an offer if they have been given one. So the main change is that students will only have the result of their applications two weeks after the end of the deadline in whichever time period they have applied (December, April or June). Otherwise, students will be processed in terms of interviews and testing as at present.      

Applications received any time after the first Friday of December (6/12/2013) will be considered in the second round and students will be notified two weeks after that session closes - the session ends the first Friday in March (7/03/2014). Again once the Admissions cut-off date is reached – all the applications that have been received and dealt with are decided upon and the students are duly informed within a two week turn around. Please note that our places will be mainly full by January therefore we strongly advise that you inform your students to submit applications in the first batch. We are very unlikely to still have places left after the second batch. 

The final student intake has to be received by the first Friday in June (6/6/2014) – by which stage most of the individual student applications will have been processed. Given the lateness of these applications once an offer has been made to the student they will need to accept or decline it within a week of receipt.

remarks:
[2 Oct 2013]
We will now be processing students in three tranches: December, April, and June.

This should work in the following way: the first deadline will be the first Friday of December of the year before entry; those students who have applied before that date will be looked at and processed in the first round.  All applications which have been received by that first Friday will be sifted through and students will have the results of their application within two weeks after cut-off date. Students will then have a week to decide whether to accept an offer if they have been given one. So the main change is that students will only have the result of their applications two weeks after the end of the deadline in whichever time period they have applied (December, April or June). Otherwise, students will be processed in terms of interviews and testing as at present.      

Applications received any time after the first Friday of December (6/12/2013) will be considered in the second round and students will be notified two weeks after that session closes - the session ends the first Friday in March (7/03/2014). Again once the Admissions cut-off date is reached – all the applications that have been received and dealt with are decided upon and the students are duly informed within a two week turn around. Please note that our places will be mainly full by January therefore we strongly advise that you inform your students to submit applications in the first batch. We are very unlikely to still have places left after the second batch. 

The final student intake has to be received by the first Friday in June (6/6/2014) – by which stage most of the individual student applications will have been processed. Given the lateness of these applications once an offer has been made to the student they will need to accept or decline it within a week of receipt.

CARDIFF 6TH FORM ENGLISH REQUIREMENT:

The college requires the student to achieve a score of 6.5 in the overall band of the ACADEMIC version of IELTS or recognised equivalent (such as an A in IGCSE English as a first Language).

remarks:
On receipt of an application:
•	The application will be acknowledged by our Admissions Secretary and logged onto our database
•	An application pack will be compiled for each student to include: 
o	The completed application form
o	Copies of the student’s latest school reports (over the previous two years)
o	Copy of the student’s passport
o	Any other information that might be helpful (copies of certificates or references for example) 
o	Results of the entry tests

Applications will then be held and assessed alongside all other applications for the same entry date in line with the following time scales:

•	Decisions for September entry will be made on 1st October (11 months prior to the entry date), i.e. applications for entry in September 2016 will be reviewed on 1st October 2015.
•	Decisions for January entry will be made on the 1st October (15 months prior to the entry date), i.e. applications for entry in January 2016 will be reviewed on 1st October 2014.  

Students will then either be offered a place to study in our GCSE or A Level classes, offered a place on the waiting list or their application will be declined.

Should any places remain available after the allocation and acceptance of offers each year; they will be offered to students who are on Concord’s waiting list or those who meet our entry criteria as they apply.

Applications which do not meet our entry criteria will be notified at the time of submission, or as soon as it is apparent that the entry criteria have not been met.

This change of policy has been driven by the increased competition for places at Concord.

This should work in the following way: the first deadline will be the first Friday of December of the year before entry; those students who have applied before that date will be looked at and processed in the first round.  All applications which have been received by that first Friday will be sifted through and students will have the results of their application within two weeks after cut-off date. Students will then have a week to decide whether to accept an offer if they have been given one. So the main change is that students will only have the result of their applications two weeks after the end of the deadline in whichever time period they have applied (December, April or June). Otherwise, students will be processed in terms of interviews and testing as at present.      

Applications received any time after the first Friday of December (6/12/2013) will be considered in the second round and students will be notified two weeks after that session closes - the session ends the first Friday in March (7/03/2014). Again once the Admissions cut-off date is reached – all the applications that have been received and dealt with are decided upon and the students are duly informed within a two week turn around. The final student intake has to be received by the first Friday in June (6/6/2014) – by which stage most of the individual student applications will have been processed. remarks: [17Dec11]Please do always send a photograph with each application form

On receipt of an application:
•	The application will be acknowledged by our Admissions Secretary and logged onto our database
•	An application pack will be compiled for each student to include: 
o	The completed application form
o	Copies of the student’s latest school reports (over the previous two years)
o	Copy of the student’s passport
o	Any other information that might be helpful (copies of certificates or references for example) 
o	Results of the entry tests

Applications will then be held and assessed alongside all other applications for the same entry date in line with the following time scales:

•	Decisions for September entry will be made on 1st October (11 months prior to the entry date), i.e. applications for entry in September 2016 will be reviewed on 1st October 2015.
•	Decisions for January entry will be made on the 1st October (15 months prior to the entry date), i.e. applications for entry in January 2016 will be reviewed on 1st October 2014.  

Students will then either be offered a place to study in our GCSE or A Level classes, offered a place on the waiting list or their application will be declined.

Should any places remain available after the allocation and acceptance of offers each year; they will be offered to students who are on Concord’s waiting list or those who meet our entry criteria as they apply.

Applications which do not meet our entry criteria will be notified at the time of submission, or as soon as it is apparent that the entry criteria have not been met.

This change of policy has been driven by the increased competition for places at Concord.

New online registration process for 16+ entry to Wellington College which we are implementing from this year onwards. 
 
In order to make registering a child for Sixth Form entry at Wellington as easy as possible, the whole process is now to be completed via a few clicks from our website.  There is a link on the 16+ Entry page (http://www.wellingtoncollege.org.uk/2575/admissions/joining-wellington/16-entry) of the Admissions section to our new online registration forms.  This will take you through to two simple forms:
 
1.     16+ Registration form to be completed by parents. This form requires simple personal details, information about pupils’ current schools, and confirmation of how to pay the registration fee.
2.     16+ Personal Statement form to be completed by pupil applicants. This form, amongst other things, requires pupils to:
•         Upload a personal statement written by them (PDF or MSWord, max. 1000 words) detailing their academic and extra-curricular strengths, their reasons for wanting to join Wellington College, and any other information which they feel will strengthen their application
•         Upload their latest set of school reports (we would suggest their reports for the Summer Term 2014)
Once both forms have been completed and the registration fee paid, we will then be able to process the application.

remarks:
On receipt of an application:
•	The application will be acknowledged by our Admissions Secretary and logged onto our database
•	An application pack will be compiled for each student to include: 
o	The completed application form
o	Copies of the student’s latest school reports (over the previous two years)
o	Copy of the student’s passport
o	Any other information that might be helpful (copies of certificates or references for example) 
o	Results of the entry tests

Applications will then be held and assessed alongside all other applications for the same entry date in line with the following time scales:

•	Decisions for September entry will be made on 1st October (11 months prior to the entry date), i.e. applications for entry in September 2016 will be reviewed on 1st October 2015.
•	Decisions for January entry will be made on the 1st October (15 months prior to the entry date), i.e. applications for entry in January 2016 will be reviewed on 1st October 2014.  

Students will then either be offered a place to study in our GCSE or A Level classes, offered a place on the waiting list or their application will be declined.

Should any places remain available after the allocation and acceptance of offers each year; they will be offered to students who are on Concord’s waiting list or those who meet our entry criteria as they apply.

Applications which do not meet our entry criteria will be notified at the time of submission, or as soon as it is apparent that the entry criteria have not been met.

This change of policy has been driven by the increased competition for places at Concord.

On receipt of an application:
•	The application will be acknowledged by our Admissions Secretary and logged onto our database
•	An application pack will be compiled for each student to include: 
o	The completed application form
o	Copies of the student’s latest school reports (over the previous two years)
o	Copy of the student’s passport
o	Any other information that might be helpful (copies of certificates or references for example) 
o	Results of the entry tests

Applications will then be held and assessed alongside all other applications for the same entry date in line with the following time scales:

•	Decisions for September entry will be made on 1st October (11 months prior to the entry date), i.e. applications for entry in September 2016 will be reviewed on 1st October 2015.
•	Decisions for January entry will be made on the 1st October (15 months prior to the entry date), i.e. applications for entry in January 2016 will be reviewed on 1st October 2014.  

Students will then either be offered a place to study in our GCSE or A Level classes, offered a place on the waiting list or their application will be declined.

Should any places remain available after the allocation and acceptance of offers each year; they will be offered to students who are on Concord’s waiting list or those who meet our entry criteria as they apply.

Applications which do not meet our entry criteria will be notified at the time of submission, or as soon as it is apparent that the entry criteria have not been met.

This change of policy has been driven by the increased competition for places at Concord.

This change of policy has been driven by the increased competition for places at Concord.

Overseas applicants to New Hall must sit the English as an Additional Language (EAL) examination, as well as entrance examinations in the A Level subjects that they wish to study. Please note that EAL is in a subject block for overseas students. Therefore, students requiring EAL will choose three subjects alongside the compulsory EAL/native language A-Level. If following the entrance assessments it is decided that a student’s English level is strong enough that they will not need to take EAL, then they may be able to choose an alternative fourth subject. Students may however sit more subject entrance examinations, in addition to EAL, if they are undecided on which three additional subjects they would like to study at this time.

remarks:
School advise early application during the Autumn Term preceding the September of entry in order to ensure boarding places are available. A reasonable level of fluency in English and good understanding of it from the outset are expected, so that the girls can access the curriculum well and make good progress. 

Registering your daughter: You will be invited to register upon receipt of a satisfactory school report. Once your daughter is registered, it is important to move towards entrance exams and interview as soon as possible, and school will keep you updated with any information regarding these exams, as well as future events at Roedean which may be of interest.

Years 7-10 & One-Year GCSE Programme: Entry is assessed by means of entrance exams in
English, Maths, and Non-Verbal Reasoning. These can be sat either at local British Council offices, at
an educational agent’s offices, or at your daughter’s current school. A Skype interview will be arranged for successful candidates to complete the admissions process.

Overseas Scholarships: Roedean is delighted to offer prestigious awards for overseas students. At Roedean, scholarships are available to new entrants to the school in order to recognise academic excellence or musical ability, in order to help extend and challenge girls to fulfil their potential; all scholars at Roedean are fully involved in our Scholars’ programme. If you wish to apply for a scholarship, please fill out the overseas scholarship application form on our website.

Academic and Music Scholarships These scholarships are available to overseas students with outstanding ability and potential, who are academically able or who are talented musicians. These are honorary scholarships which carry a small award for scholarship-related activities.

If Tonbridge is happy with the interview performance, the school will encourage your child to complete the application form and pay the application fee and attend the entrance exam in Nov 2021, the entrance exam is the same exam as those who received the conditional offer in 2019. Result will be released in Dec 2021.

Years 7-10 & One-Year GCSE Programme: Entry is assessed by means of entrance exams in
English, Maths, and Non-Verbal Reasoning. These can be sat either at local British Council offices, at
an educational agent’s offices, or at your daughter’s current school. A Skype interview will be arranged for successful candidates to complete the admissions process.

Overseas Scholarships: Roedean is delighted to offer prestigious awards for overseas students. At Roedean, scholarships are available to new entrants to the school in order to recognise academic excellence or musical ability, in order to help extend and challenge girls to fulfil their potential; all scholars at Roedean are fully involved in our Scholars’ programme. If you wish to apply for a scholarship, please fill out the overseas scholarship application form on our website.

Academic and Music Scholarships These scholarships are available to overseas students with outstanding ability and potential, who are academically able or who are talented musicians. These are honorary scholarships which carry a small award for scholarship-related activities.

remarks:
School advise early application during the Autumn Term preceding the September of entry in order to ensure boarding places are available. A reasonable level of fluency in English and good understanding of it from the outset are expected, so that the girls can access the curriculum well and make good progress. Applicants to Year 12 and our One-Year GCSE Programme are expected to be working at the equivalent of IELTS 6.5-7 (CEFR C1) in English.

Registering your daughter: You will be invited to register upon receipt of a satisfactory school report. Once your daughter is registered, it is important to move towards entrance exams and interview as soon as possible, and school will keep you updated with any information regarding these exams, as well as future events at Roedean which may be of interest.
Year 12: Entry is assessed by means of entrance exams in English, Maths, and Non-Verbal Reasoning. Non-native speakers also sit the Oxford Online Placement Test. These can be sat either at local British Council offices, at an educational agent’s offices, or at your daughter’s current school. A Skype interview will be arranged for successful candidates to complete the admissions process. At a later point, after the place has been accepted, students will choose three subjects they would like to study at A Level and sit a 30 minute paper in each of these. This will help place students on the best A Level Programme of Study for them, and will help us to assess whether any academic provision or preparation will be required ahead of the September start.

Overseas Scholarships: Roedean is delighted to offer prestigious awards for overseas students. At Roedean, scholarships are available to new entrants to the school in order to recognise academic excellence or musical ability, in order to help extend and challenge girls to fulfil their potential; all scholars at Roedean are fully involved in our Scholars’ programme. If you wish to apply for a scholarship, please fill out the overseas scholarship application form on our website.

Newnham Scholarships (Year 12 only)
The Newnham Scholarships are the highest and most fiercely-competitive academic award available at Roedean, worth 10% of full boarding fees, and all are awarded based on performance in the entrance tests, assessments if relevant, and interview. The Newnham Scholarships are awarded to the best international boarding applicants. 

Academic and Music Scholarships These scholarships are available to overseas students with outstanding ability and potential, who are academically able or who are talented musicians. These are honorary scholarships which carry a small award for scholarship-related activities.

Application Procedure:
Apply 3 years before the entry year:
Apply before 30 June 2021, complete reg form and pay the fee, attend ISEB CE Pre-Test on or before 30 Nov 2021 in HK, if the school is happy with the ISEB Common Pre-Test score, your child will be invited to go to the UK to attend the Tonbridge Assessment  either in Nov 2021 if students take ISEB early or Jan 2022,  if passed the Tonbridge Assessment, your child will be offered a conditional place subject to passing Eng and Math test in 2023 or unconditional place without further testing. For late applicants missed the above application timeframe, application and ISEB Common Pre-Test can be completed before end of May 2022.

Apply 1 year before the entry year:
Attend Academic Asia Screening Test and reach the benchmark required by Tonbridge School,  if reached the benchmark, AA will arrange your child to attend the interview in Top Schools Weekend in Sep 2023 when Tonbridge comes to HK. If Tonbridge is happy with the interview performance, the school will encourage your child to complete the application form and pay the application fee and attend the entrance exam in Nov 2023, the entrance exam is the same exam as those who received the conditional offer in 2020. Result will be released in Dec 2023.
